summary.deep: In India, the Cockroach movement felt the crushing boot of the state this week. Thousands of Gen Z protesters were rounded up and detained in sports stadiums and community halls turned into makeshift detention centres, while the movement’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, was arrested on arrival. A mass demonstration over alleged voter fraud was effectively crushed before it could begin.And Abdijeet has been detained again todayNarendra Modi’s government says the measures were necessary to protect civilians in the capital. But he now faces accusations of choosing repression over democracy, with the UN Human Rights Office urging authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly.

QR codes are not proprietary technology; they are governed by open, decades-old standards formally defined by ISO/IEC 18004. This standard details deterministic algorithms for data encoding and error correction using Reed-Solomon codes. When companies act as URL shorteners and proxies through paid SaaS platforms, they introduce vendor lock-in, recurring subscription costs, and privacy concerns regarding tracked traffic. Modern web browsers possess sufficient capabilities and mathematical libraries to generate QR codes locally using vanilla JavaScript, rendering monthly subscription fees for basic generation entirely unnecessary.
summary.std: Software developers are questioning why dynamic QR code SaaS startups charge high monthly subscription fees for basic functionalities. Instead of relying on proprietary proxy servers that create vendor lock-in, developers can generate QR codes directly within modern web browsers using JavaScript.

article.headline: Misconfigured cache header inadvertently caches authentication redirects for a year
article.keyFact: A routing-layer rule misapplied a one-year immutable cache header to authentication redirect responses.

summary.brief: A static asset cache configuration error caused authentication redirect responses to be cached with an immutable one-year header.
summary.deep: A website's Next.js configuration included a static asset caching rule designed to apply an aggressive one-year immutable cache control header to files under a specific static path. However, because the site did not actually contain a static directory at that location, any incoming requests to that route were handled by the site's authorization gate, resulting in a redirect response to the login page. Since headers() matches URL routing patterns rather than validating physical file existence, the server stamped the one-year immutable header onto the authentication redirect response. Consequently, browsers were instructed to cache the sign-in redirect for a full year without revalidation, while actual static assets like the site logo defaulted to standard revalidation rules.
summary.std: A routing-layer configuration rule intended to cache static assets aggressively with a one-year immutable header was misapplied. Because the rule matched paths rather than files and the target path did not exist, requests to non-existent static paths triggered authentication redirects to a sign-in page, causing browsers to store the login redirect for a full year.
